articles.title: How Democrats Can Start the Next Era of Immigration Reform Now
articles.summary: The 2026 midterm election results rebuked President Donald Trump’s failures on the economy and, in several competitive races, his immigration agenda. Latino voters who backed him in 2024 swung back to Democrats, helping deliver the politically unthinkable. Texas elected its first Democratic senator since 1988 and its first Latina governor , while Democrats won governorships in all four southern border states and every southern border congressional district. articles.title: How Movies About Tech Turned Dystopian
articles.summary: In 2014, a film about a prickly, arrogant inventor trying to build a “machine that can solve any problem” arrived in theaters. It explored the secretive creation of a powerful technology that enabled a group of military leaders to unilaterally determine the life and death of thousands. From the vantage point of 2026, the story sounds unsettling, even dystopian. articles.title: A New Pill Could Reduce the Risk of Having a Second Stroke
articles.summary: On November 9, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a new type of medication to reduce the risk of strokes in certain populations. Asundexian, which will be sold under the brand name Sunharbo, is a daily pill that is the first to target a specific factor in the blood-clotting process that can contribute to stroke.
